visuals.heading: Get the Skill Stack and the Proof

items.text: Get the skill stack and the proof of coverage right, and this path can move you toward earlier financial freedom faster than the entry-level pay suggests.

Strip away the "media and events" branding and the job is this: you manage what gets said about a person, brand, or organisation, through people who are not on your payroll, journalists, editors, influencers, and industry voices, instead of through ads the brand pays for directly.
None of that is as glamorous as it sounds in a job description.
The "big win" moments - a front-page story, a trending influencer post, a well-handled crisis, happen occasionally and briefly.
Every "how to get into PR" guide eventually reduces to three real doors.
A BA in Mass Communication, Journalism, or Public Relations, followed by a PG diploma or MA in Public Relations or Corporate Communication.
You are choosing a degree now and want a direct, recognised path with placement support and campus internships built in.

blocks.heading: AI Is Actually Doing to PR Work

items.text: This is not a future risk, it is already showing up in the numbers.

The more useful framing is not "will AI replace PR professionals" but "what changes about what a PR professional actually does." A junior executive today can supervise AI tooling to produce drafts and research that once took two or three people working manually, which raises the bar for what a junior hire is expected to add on top: judgment, accuracy checking, and relationship-building that AI cannot fake.
This makes the entry bar higher, not lower.

blocks.heading: Three Proofs Before You Apply Anywhere

items.text: Before your first real PR application, run yourself through the same three proofs that decide whether anyone is willing to trust you with a real client's story.
Three real tests stand between "interested in PR" and "ready to be hired into PR."
Can you write a real press release and a real media pitch, cold.

blocks.heading: Mistakes That Stall People in PR

items.text: Most of the actual week is writing, research, follow-up emails, and coverage tracking.
A pitch that clearly was not written for the specific journalist gets ignored, and repeat offenders get quietly blacklisted by beat reporters.
A PR professional who can only pitch traditional print and TV media is competing for a shrinking slice of client budgets.

Owns client relationships, sets campaign strategy, manages junior staff, handles early-stage crisis situations.
Multi-account or category oversight, new business pitching, senior client counsel, budget ownership.
Practice leadership, C-suite client counsel, crisis command, agency or team P&L responsibility.

blocks.heading: Skills That Actually Get You Hired
rows: Press releases, pitches, statements, and briefing notes have to be accurate and fast, this is the single most tested skill in every PR interview.
A journalist who trusts you returns your calls. This is built slowly through relevant, non-spammy pitching, not a media list you bought or scraped.
The work that actually separates a PR professional from a content writer, staying calm, accurate, and fast when a story turns negative.
Modern PR briefs routinely include an influencer or creator layer alongside traditional media, so understanding platforms, rates, and disclosure norms is now baseline, not a bonus.
Clients increasingly ask for share of voice, sentiment, and message pull-through data, not just a clipping count, basic spreadsheet and analytics comfort now matters.
Using AI for first-draft releases, media list research, and monitoring, then checking the output for accuracy and tone before anything goes out under a client's name.

blocks.heading: What PR Professionals Actually Earn
rows: Rs 2-4 LPA (agency); Rs 3-5 LPA (in-house, when hired directly)
Many agencies pay a stipend during a 3-6 month internship before converting to a full-time offer at the lower end of this band.
This is where most PR careers actually start earning a stable salary, the gap between agency and in-house pay is usually smallest at this stage.
The band widens sharply here based on sector: fintech, healthcare, and tech clients tend to pay more than lifestyle or FMCG accounts at the same seniority.
In-house corporate communications roles at large or listed companies commonly sit at the top of this band, especially where investor relations overlaps with the role.
At this level, pay depends heavily on whether the role is agency leadership (linked to new-business billings) or a corporate communications head role reporting to a CEO or board.

blocks.heading: Pay By City and Agency Type
rows: The two largest PR hubs, most agency head offices and the highest concentration of national media sit here, which also means the most competition for entry-level seats.
Typically the top of every experience band above; cost of living also runs highest.
Strong for tech, startup, and product PR specifically, with agencies and in-house teams built around fast-growing companies and investor-facing communication.
Close to Mumbai/Delhi at mid-to-senior levels, especially for startup and tech-sector accounts.
Regional PR now accounts for roughly 19% of industry revenue, up from about 10% three years ago, as brands push beyond metro-only coverage. Pay is lower, but so is competition for the first job.
Usually the lower end of each experience band, with faster ownership of real client work.
